description: Echos of Earth is a team led by women across Brazil who are interested in learning and science. The project focuses on exploring Mars while discovering five Martian rovers. Our shared passion drove us to create “Wonder” — created by young minds for young minds. Join us to meet Wonder!
summary: Echos of Earth was born from the idea of building a new explorer using salvaged modules from multiple generations of spacecraft. Each part preserves the identity and memory of its original mission. The project turns technical data into playable content—blending exploration stories, collectible hardware, assembly mechanics, narrative choices, and scientific discoveries. All sources listed in our submission come from official documentation and archives by NASA/JPL, ESA, DLR, and NIST. It is important to note that while the roleplay imagines recovering and reusing old components, this is strictly a narrative device. Instead, this concept is framed as a fictional reconstruction grounded in authentic engineering roles and architectures. Planetary exploration leaves behind a wide variety of artifacts: rovers, landers, descent stages, science platforms, deployed instruments, lunar vehicles, retroreflectors, impact probes, and jettisoned landing gear. While some systems have gone silent, others remain passively active, aiding ongoing measurements, and a few were intentionally crashed. Every item’s story is shaped by its purpose, environment, and available data. Our goal was to use a playful approach and accessible language to keep younger audiences engaged—building a welcoming bridge between science and education.
details:
Echos of Earth is a project designed to teach young audiences about NASA equipment left behind on Mars, using accessible language and engaging mechanics. Our goal is to attract and include more youth in science, making it feel relatable rather than out of reach.

To code and deploy the app, we used Claude AI—an AI-powered platform that translates program ideas into functional software. Although the platform utilizes artificial intelligence, every prompt written inside Claude was entirely conceived and drafted by our team without AI assistance.

From the very beginning, we created the artwork, wrote the vast majority of the text, and manually verified all factual data. The core game concept and characters are completely original to our team. While we used AI as a supplementary tool to organize information, clarify complex concepts, and proofread translations and spelling, all research, source curation, critical analysis, fact-checking, and creative decisions were strictly human-led.
